searchText: John Adler uses the term "non-consensus node". This is friendly to PoW and PoW too. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=l4jccXoqLGM&t=197s It seems plausible for there to be schemes with partial statefulness (e.g. 5% of state is held locally) that're still participating in staking, especially if there's a proliferation of staking services (e.g. many oceanic stakers each watching a portion of Rocketpool validators). What does "non-consensus node" mean exactly? All 4 combinations listed above can follow consensus. Under PBS, you don't need state to be a staker. Portal network is building something where not everyone will hold everything. In this case I believe it's a node that can follow consensus, but doesn't propose blocks or provide attestations. So anyone but a miner/staker? Purely passive would imply not participating in transaction and block gossip I think. That's how I interpret it!
